title: Direct-Contact Co-culture of Astrocytes and Glioblastoma Cells Patterned using Polyelectrolyte Multilayer Templates
protocol: Obtain a master pattern of desired geometry before beginning this protocol.
Prepare buffers and media for cell culture.
Prepare poly(diallylmethylammonium chloride) (PDAC) coating solution which is 0.3 wt. % PDAC and 0.1 M NaCl in ddH2O.
Prepare sulfonated poly(sterene) (SPS) polymer solution which is 30 µM SPS and 0.1 M NaCl in ddH2O.
Obtain or prepare standard cell culture media, if needed.
Typical astrocyte medium is 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM).
Thaw cells as required for the experiment.
Weigh 12 parts PDMS pre-polymer and 1 part curing agent in a disposable container.
Mix the PDMS mixture vigorously for 2-4 min until bubbles form throughout.
Place fluorosilane into the fluorosilane desiccator.
Place the disposable container with the polymer mixture into the desiccator to degas for 20 min.
Place the pre-patterned structure master into a Petri dish.
Pour the PDMS mixture slowly over the pre-patterned structure master, ensuring complete coverage.
Keep the Petri dish in a fluorosilane desiccator to remove bubbles.
Cure the PDMS layer at 60 °C for 1 hour or at 37 °C overnight if higher temperature is not available.
Cut around the master using a sharp scalpel evenly and gently.
Remove the stamp using tweezers and place it on a cutting surface.
Cut the stamps into sizes suitable for 6-well plates (approximately 2.5 cm x 2.5 cm).
Plasma-clean a 6-well plate for 7 minutes.
Bleed the chamber by turning the three-way valve on the front of the door to the right until a hiss from the air release can be heard.
Turn the three-way valve back to the vertical position once the pressure reading is above 1800 mTorr.
Open the door and place the 6-well plate in the chamber.
Close the door and turn on the vacuum pump.
Evacuate the chamber until the pressure stabilizes around 100 mTorr.
Confirm that the oxygen tank is open, and the output pressure of the oxygen is 10 psi.
Open the three-way valve to the left to align it with the oxygen input hose.
Allow oxygen gas to bleed into the chamber until the pressure stabilizes between 400 and 450 mTorr.
Confirm that the input pressure on the flow meter is 10 mm and adjust if needed.
Turn on the RF power.
Wait for the plasma to form (~15 s).
Start the timer for 7 min.
After 7 min, turn off the RF power.
Turn the three-way valve back to its vertical position.
Allow the chamber to evacuate to 150 mTorr.
Turn off the vacuum pump and wait for the pressure to rise to 1500 mTorr.
Vent the chamber by turning the three-way valve to the right until a hiss from the air release can be heard.
When the pressure reading is above 1800 mTorr, turn the three-way valve back to its vertical position.
Open the door and retrieve the sample.
Place plasma coated plates in room temperature baths for PDAC for 20 min, DI water for 5 min, DI water for 5 min, SPS for 20 min, DI water for 5 min, and DI water for 5 min.
Repeat the washing step a total of 10 times.
Allow the plates to air dry.
Wash PDMS stamps with gentle lab soap followed by DI water.
Dry the stamps using an air compressor and place them on a flat surface such as an unused 6-well plate lid.
Plasma coat the stamps for 1 min.
Place the plasma-coated stamps face down on prepared 6-well plates.
Pipette 10 µL of PDAC solution along the bottom edge of the stamp, dispensing steadily along its length.
Add a 350 g weight on top of each stamp for 20 s to enforce the pattern.
Allow the stamps to rest on the plates for 20 min.
Dip the plate into DI water and peel off the stamps in the direction of the line patterns.
Wash the plate twice for 5 min each in DI water.
Wash the stamps with soap and DI water and dry with an air compressor.
Allow the plate to air dry.
Sterilize the plates under UV light in a Class II biosafety hood for a minimum of 8 h immediately prior to use if ready for cell culture.
Visualize stamped patterns with carboxyfluorescein (CFSE) if not using the patterns for cell culture.
Place dried, stamped patterns in CFSE pattern staining solution (0.1 µM CFSE in 0.1 M NaOH) for 60-90 min.
Wash stamped patterns for 5 min in DI H2O two times.
Visualize patterns using an appropriate fluorescence microscope.
Turn on the fluorescent bulb to allow it to warm up for 10 minutes.
Use the interference blue filter (IB) to visualize green patterns.
Take photos of the patterns.
Detach glioblastoma cells from the culture surface with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge detached cells at 200 x g for 4 minutes at 4 °C and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL cell culture media without serum, centrifuge at 200 x g for 4 minutes at 4 °C, then remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS and transfer to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Add 10 µL of 10 µg/mL CFSE to the cell suspension.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down immediately after adding CFSE.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Transfer into a 15 mL sterile tube.
Quench the CFSE dye reaction by adding a minimum of 1 mL of cell culture medium.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 5 mL of cell culture medium and transfer to a fresh 15 mL sterile tube.
Centrifuge resuspended cells at 400 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C, then remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells once again in 5 mL of cell culture medium.
Repeat the previous wash step twice.
Seed the stained glioma cells (100 cells/mm² or 100,000 cells/well) in the patterned 6-well tissue culture plate from step 4 with astrocyte culture media.
Culture the cells in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂) for 24 h before adding stained astrocytes in step 7.
Perform all cell culture work in a suitable Class II biosafety cabinet.
Detach cells from the culture surface with 0.25% trypsin-EDTA.
Centrifuge detached cells at 200 x g for 4 min at 4 °C and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of cell culture media without serum (DMEM and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Centrifuge resuspended cells at 200 x g for 4 min at 4 °C and remove supernatant.
Prepare a 2x cell suspension by resuspending the cell pellet in 0.5 mL of room temperature Diluent C from the PKH26 kit.
Prepare a 2x dye solution (4 x 10⁻⁶ M) by adding 2 µL of PKH26 to 0.5 mL of Diluent C in a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Add 2x cell suspension to 2x dye solution and immediately mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the cell suspension for 1-5 min.
Quench staining by adding a minimum 5x volume of the cell culture medium and incubating for 1 min to bind excess dye.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 10 min at 4 °C and carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of cell culture media and transfer to a new sterile 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min at 4 °C, remove the supernatant and resuspend in 5 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min at 4 °C, remove the supernatant and resuspend in 5 mL of cell culture media.
Repeat steps 7.9 and 7.10 for a total of three washes.
Seed the stained astrocytes (200 cells/mm² or 200,000 cells/well) with astrocyte media in the patterned 6-well tissue culture plate pre-seeded with glioma cells.
Culture the cells in 37 °C, 5% CO₂ incubator for the duration of the experiments.
Turn on the fluorescent bulb to allow it to warm up for 10 min.
Remove the cell culture from the incubator and set it on the stage of an inverted microscope capable of fluorescence imaging.
Insert or attach the appropriate filter.
If the cells being imaged are stained with CFSE, use the interference blue filter (IB) to visualize the green cells.
If the cells being imaged are stained with PKH26, use a Rhodamine filter to visualize the red cells.
View the specimen and take photos.
